name: platform_identity_discovery
description: Two additive /health members beside `tier` and `version` that say WHICH BUILD of AxonFlow, configured WHICH WAY, is answering: `edition` (`community` | `enterprise`, from the binary's own build tag, so it is a fact about the compilation and not about the licence) and `deployment_mode` (this deployment's own DEPLOYMENT_MODE setting, resolved to its canonical spelling with aliases folded — `enterprise` reports as `in-vpc-enterprise`). Served identically on the agent (8080) and orchestrator (8081) planes from one implementation (platform/shared/heartbeat.HealthIdentityMembers), so a client that probes whichever port it can reach gets the same answer - agent-vs-orchestrator /health drift is failure mode 1 in RUNBOOK_RELEASE_PREP.md and has happened in a real train, which is why this is one function rather than two literals. ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY: a member the platform cannot determine is OMITTED, never present with an empty value — `deployment_mode` is absent when DEPLOYMENT_MODE is unset, and that absence is a real observation (`the operator configured nothing`) which must not be read as the `community` default the SCHEMA selector applies, because the RUNTIME posture for an unset value is not community. A RELAYING CLIENT MUST MAP THIS `deployment_mode` ONTO THE TELEMETRY FIELD `platform_deployment_mode`, NOT ONTO THE FIELD OF THE SAME NAME ON A PING, which is the coarse topology (self_hosted | community_saas) the SDK derives from its own endpoint URL — the two are different dimensions and conflating them corrupts every existing deployment-mode dashboard. NEITHER MEMBER IS AN ENTITLEMENT FACT: whoever operates the endpoint controls both values completely, so they are adoption analytics only and must never gate a feature, an authorization decision or a billing decision (#3660, #3619 trust boundary)
